name: standing iron brazier seen from above at 3/4: wide round fire bowl full of glowing coals with flames, on a tall tripod stand
label: pirate-isles/pi-torch-stand

answer.evidence: The brazier bowl opens toward the viewer with a visible 4-row elliptical interior (rows 8-11) filled with glowing coals and fire, showing proper 3/4 top-down foreshortening rather than a flat side profile.

answer.main_body: round fire bowl atop a tripod stand
answer.evidence: The fire bowl opening is foreshortened and clearly viewed from above at a 3/4 angle, showing 5 rows of glowing coals/fire bed (rows 7-11) inside the circular rim before the front wall of the bowl drops down (rows 12-15).

The round fire bowl opening is foreshortened as an ellipse (rows 7 to 11, roughly 5 rows tall) filled with glowing coals and flames, viewed from above before curving down into the bowl's south exterior wall and tripod base.

The top opening of the fire bowl is drawn foreshortened with the glowing coal bed visible inside across rows 7-11 (5 rows tall), with the front exterior wall of the bowl extending below it across rows 12-15.
